report.source_text: Histological analysis showed proliferation of the chorion in the form of small nests with relatively uniform, medium-sized cells and rounded to polyhedral cells containing homogenous, ovoid nuclei with fine chromatin. It was associated with numerous thin-walled vascular structures, lined by endothelial cells without atypia. The tumour cells containing a cytoplasmic frame well defined by reticulin were positive for actin and caldesmone with low expression for CD99. There was no expression for pancytokeratins, CD34, chromogranin, synaptophysin, S100 protein, SOX-10, desmin or inhibin. There also was no signs of malignancy.

report.source_text: The patient underwent volumetric intensity by arc therapy radiation at a total dose of 53 Gy over 25 sessions, with a frequency of five sessions per week. He was kept hospitalised during this period. The treatment was well tolerated without side effects or complications. He remained stable without either recurrence of bleeding or respiratory distress.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An early 80s male with active smoking history presented with massive haemoptysis and respiratory distress preceded by self-resolving bloody sputum episodes. Emergency endoscopy revealed a large bleeding tracheal tumour obstructing ~90% of the lumen, necessitating intubation and surgical tracheotomy. CT imaging demonstrated a 25mm posterior subcricoid tracheal mass with arterial phase contrast enhancement, infiltration of intertracheoesophageal fat, and mass effect on the oesophagus without metastatic disease. Histopathological examination of the mass revealed nests of uniform medium-sized cells with perivascular myoid differentiation surrounding thin-walled vascular channels, with immunohistochemistry positive for smooth muscle markers (actin, caldesmone) and negative for epithelial (pancytokeratins), vascular (CD34), neuroendocrine (chromogranin, synaptophysin), and melanocytic (S100, SOX-10) markers, confirming glomangioma. The patient underwent definitive radiation therapy (53 Gy over 25 sessions) with good tolerance and remained stable without recurrence of bleeding or respiratory distress.
